reports.title: Host Hotels & Resorts, Inc. Reports Results for the Third Quarter of 2026

guidance.heading: 2026 OUTLOOK
section: In the third quarter of 2026, the Company continued to see strong leisure and group demand, which drove an increase in rates, coupled with improving business transient volume. Comparable hotel RevPAR for October also grew approximately 6.5% over 2025. The updated 2026 guidance reflects the Company's strong third quarter results and improved expectations for the fourth quarter driven by strong leisure demand, favorable group booking pace, and improving business transient demand. Full year operating profit margins and comparable hotel EBITDA margins are expected to increase compared to 2025, as rate improvements offset increases in wage expense.

The guidance includes an estimated $3 million and $6 million of net income and Adjusted EBITDAre, respectively, which is expected from the recent acquisitions of 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge and Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West Hotel. Due to the timing of the acquisitions, the results for these two hotels will be included in comparable hotel results starting in the fourth quarter. The guidance for net income and Adjusted EBITDAre also includes an estimated $18 million net contribution from sales expected to close at the condominium development adjacent to the Four Seasons Resort Orlando at Walt Disney World® Resort this year, with remaining sales expected to shift into 2027. Additionally, the final determination on insurance claims related to Hurricanes Helene and Milton is expected by the end of the year, but no additional amounts from what was received in first quarter are included in guidance.

desk.headline: Adjusted FFO up 11% to $0.39 a share, just above estimates; full-year 2026 outlook raised again
results: Revenue per available room at comparable hotels rose 8.8%, with room rates up 5.7% and occupancy up 2.1 points; the World Cup and more business travel helped.
Reported revenue rose only 1.2% to $1.35bn because hotels sold in 2025 and 2026 no longer count.
Adjusted funds from operations (the main REIT profit measure) rose to $0.39 a share from $0.35; GAAP profit fell to $0.10 a share as last year included large gains on hotel sales.
After the quarter Host bought the 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge ($202m) and the Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West ($172m), and extended its $2.5bn credit facility to 2031–2032.
It paid a quarterly dividend of $0.20 a share on 15 October.

guidance.summary: Host lifted its 2026 outlook for the fourth time this year, now expecting comparable RevPAR growth of about 6.75% and adjusted FFO of about $2.21 a share. October RevPAR was up about 6.5%.

points: Business travel picked up through the quarter, with business room nights up 8.5% in August.
Group bookings are running ahead of last year, with fourth-quarter group business up about 10%; 2027 must lap the World Cup boost.
Wage rates are still rising about 5%, limiting how much extra revenue reaches profit.
Hawaii storms cut about $10m from full-year EBITDA; Maui RevPAR still rose 13.5% in the quarter.
Management hinted at another privately negotiated hotel purchase within 60 to 90 days.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99.1) and Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether fourth-quarter RevPAR keeps up the October pace of about 6.5%.
Wage growth versus room-rate gains, and its effect on margins.
Any further hotel purchases or sales, and how 2027 group bookings hold up after the World Cup.
